title: Construct the normalized coefficient inverse-image comparison on hearts
statement: Construct the normalized coefficient inverse-image comparison on hearts. For a commutative topological ring A, a condensed commutative ring R, a ring-object isomorphism e:R ≅ coefficient(A), and normalized encodings EX,EY, heart(e,T,E) is restriction of scalars along coefficientMap(e.inv,T), followed by sectionEncoding(A,T,E.ringIso) and fixedRestriction(A,T). The Encoding equations identify this concrete functor with the supplied ordinary and fixed equivalence functors. For every scheme morphism f:X→Y, heartPull is a specified natural isomorphism upperStar(R,f);heart(e,X,EX) ≅ heart(e,Y,EY);upperStar(A,f). Its inverse is the mate of heartPush, the identity-on-sections direct-image comparison. Once the normalized encodings are supplied, this construction needs no separate finiteness or discreteness hypothesis.

source.place: Transport and clause (2); inverse-image coefficient encoding, steps 1--3.

proof.text: Use the proved normalized sectionPushforward_smul to construct the identity linear isomorphism on sections and its naturality. Compose it with the published comapLowerStarIso for e.inv to obtain heartPush.

Restriction along a ring isomorphism is an equivalence. Hence the heart encodings are equivalences. The inverse mate of heartPush is invertible: take its mate again along the encoding equivalences, use the iterated-mate conjugation identity, and reflect invertibility through conjugation. Define heartPull as its inverse. The mate equation is the inverse law of mateEquiv.

      heart A R e Y EY ⋙ upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) f
